types.name: strategies.v1.Backtest
types.doc: Backtest is one backtest of a version.

fields.name: backtest_id
fields.doc: Public backtest ID.

fields.name: version_id
fields.doc: The version backtested.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: Current status.

fields.name: window
fields.doc: The simulated window.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When the backtest was started.

fields.name: finished_at
fields.doc: When it finished or failed. Omitted before.

fields.name: report
fields.doc: The result. Set only when status is DONE.

fields.name: failure
fields.doc: Why it failed. Empty unless status is FAILED.

fields.name: attempts
fields.doc:
Backtests the caller ran so far of this bot's versions. Many attempts
 make a good result more likely to be luck.

fields.name: not_backtestable_reason
fields.doc:
Why the bot cannot be backtested. Set only when status is
 NOT_BACKTESTABLE.

types.name: strategies.v1.BacktestLimitDetail
types.doc:
BacktestLimitDetail is a caller's backtest limits and how much of them is
 used, as BACKTEST_LIMIT_REACHED reports them: daily_used reaching
 daily_limit is the daily limit, and retry_after says when the UTC day
 resets; active reaching active_limit is the limit at once, and a slot frees
 when one finishes.

fields.name: daily_limit
fields.doc: Backtests the caller may start per UTC day.

fields.name: daily_used
fields.doc: Backtests the caller started in the current UTC day.

fields.name: active_limit
fields.doc: Backtests the caller may have queued or running at once.

fields.name: active
fields.doc: Backtests the caller has queued or running.

types.name: strategies.v1.BacktestMetrics
types.doc: BacktestMetrics are the results of a bot over one period.

fields.name: return_percent
fields.doc: Return over the period, in percent, for example "4.2" or "-1.5".

fields.name: max_drawdown_percent
fields.doc: Largest fall from a peak, in percent.

fields.name: trades
fields.doc: Trades made.

fields.name: win_rate_percent
fields.doc: Share of closed trades that made a profit, in percent.

fields.name: fees
fields.doc: Fees paid, in the quote asset.

fields.name: exposure_percent
fields.doc: Share of the period the bot held a position, in percent.

fields.name: sharpe_ratio
fields.doc:
Annualized Sharpe ratio of the daily returns, with a zero risk-free rate,
 for example "1.4". Unset when undefined: with fewer than two daily
 returns, or when they never vary.

fields.name: realized_pnl
fields.doc:
Profit and loss realized by the period's sells, in the quote asset, after
 their fees. Signed base-10 decimal string, for example "12.5" or
 "-3.25".

fields.name: max_drawdown_start
fields.doc: When the largest fall started: its peak.

fields.name: max_drawdown_end
fields.doc: When the largest fall ended: its trough.

fields.name: start_equity
fields.doc:
Equity at the period's start, exactly, as an exact decimal in the quote
 asset: the equity curve is sampled, so read the bounds here. For the
 tuning period (or the whole window without a split) it is the initial
 balances, any base asset valued at the reference open of the window's
 first bar. For the held-back period it is the equity at the split, the
 open position marked at the last close before it.

fields.name: end_equity
fields.doc:
Equity at the period's end, exactly, as an exact decimal in the quote
 asset: the equity at the period's last close, an open position marked at
 that close.

types.name: strategies.v1.BacktestReport
types.doc:
BacktestReport is the result of a finished backtest. Only bots that trade
 with market orders, including exits on watched price levels, are
 backtested. Every amount is in the bot's markets' one quote asset. The
 results below are for the base cost scenario; scenarios gives the range.

fields.name: fidelity
fields.doc:
What was simulated and how, as a short label naming every assumption:
 the candles, the reference prices, the spread and slippage, when orders
 fill, the fees and the starting balance.

fields.name: period
fields.doc:
The period the bot was tuned on. With a window too short to hold months
 back, it is the whole window.

fields.name: held_back_period
fields.doc:
The most recent months, held back from tuning. Unset when the window is
 too short to hold months back.

fields.name: metrics
fields.doc: Results over period.

fields.name: held_back_metrics
fields.doc: Results over held_back_period. Unset without one.

fields.name: baselines
fields.doc: The baselines over period: buy-and-hold and cash.

fields.name: trades
fields.doc:
The first trades of the whole window, oldest first: at most 20.
 ListBacktestTrades lists all of them.

fields.name: data_gaps
fields.doc: Spans without market data, oldest first.

fields.name: warnings
fields.doc: What to keep in mind when reading the result.

fields.name: evidence_grade
fields.doc: How much the result can be trusted.

fields.name: held_back_baselines
fields.doc: The baselines over held_back_period. Empty without one.

fields.name: scenarios
fields.doc:
The result under each cost scenario, low, base and high: the range to
 read, never one exact number.

fields.name: equity
fields.doc:
The equity curve over the whole window, with buy-and-hold's, at most
 1,000 points, oldest first. It is sampled, but always holds the peaks and
 troughs of every largest fall reported.

fields.name: held_back_start
fields.doc: Where held_back_period starts on the curve. Unset without one.

fields.name: window_max_drawdown_percent
fields.doc: The largest fall over the whole window, in percent.

fields.name: window_max_drawdown_start
fields.doc: When the whole window's largest fall started: its peak.

fields.name: window_max_drawdown_end
fields.doc: When the whole window's largest fall ended: its trough.

fields.name: held_back_seen
fields.doc:
True when the caller's earlier backtests already showed part of
 held_back_period, so it is no longer excluded from tuning.

types.name: strategies.v1.BacktestScenario
types.doc: BacktestScenario is a backtest's result under one cost scenario.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The scenario: low, base or high.

fields.name: slippage_bps
fields.doc: Slippage per side, in basis points.

fields.name: metrics
fields.doc: Results over the report's period.

fields.name: held_back_metrics
fields.doc: Results over the report's held-back period. Unset without one.

types.name: strategies.v1.BacktestSummary
types.doc: BacktestSummary is the headline of a version's latest backtest.

fields.name: backtest_id
fields.doc: Public backtest ID.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: Its status.

fields.name: metrics
fields.doc: Results over the tuning period. Set only when status is DONE.

fields.name: held_back_metrics
fields.doc: Results over the held-back period. Set only when status is DONE.

fields.name: attempts
fields.doc: Backtests run so far for this bot's family of versions.

types.name: strategies.v1.BacktestTrade
types.doc: BacktestTrade is one trade a backtest made.

fields.name: time
fields.doc: When the trade happened, in simulated time.

fields.name: market
fields.doc: Market, for example BTC-USDT.

fields.name: side
fields.doc: Side.

fields.name: price
fields.doc: Price, as an exact decimal in the quote asset.

fields.name: quantity
fields.doc: Quantity, as an exact decimal in the base asset.

fields.name: fee
fields.doc: Fee paid.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: The reason the bot gave for the order.

fields.name: realized_pnl
fields.doc:
Profit and loss this trade realized, in the quote asset, after its fee.
 Signed base-10 decimal string, for example "4.1" or "-0.75". Empty on a
 buy, which only opens or adds to a position.

fields.name: trade_index
fields.doc:
The trade's position among the backtest's trades, numbered from 0 in
 the order they filled. ListBacktestTrades pages in this order.

fields.name: after_gap
fields.doc:
True when the market data the order would have filled on was missing,
 so it filled at the first price after the gap.

types.name: strategies.v1.Baseline
types.doc: Baseline is a simple strategy a backtest is compared with.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Baseline name: buy_and_hold or cash.

fields.name: metrics
fields.doc: Its results over the same period.

types.name: strategies.v1.Bot
types.doc: Bot is one bot of the caller.

fields.name: bot_id
fields.doc: Public bot ID.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The bot's name, as approved when the bot was deployed.

fields.name: subaccount_id
fields.doc:
Public ID of the bot's own subaccount, which the caller's main account
 owns.

Public ID. ConnectRPC carries it as fixed64 (a decimal string in JSON).

fields.name: status
fields.doc: Current state.

fields.name: status_reason
fields.doc:
Why the bot paused, in words: the bot's own message when it decided
 to pause, else a sentence for pause_reason. Set only with PAUSED.

fields.name: version_id
fields.doc: The version it runs.

fields.name: last_decision_at
fields.doc:
When the bot last decided: the time of the event behind its newest
 decision, over all its deployments. Omitted before its first decision.
 Lags the bot by up to about a minute.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When the bot was deployed.

fields.name: quote_asset
fields.doc: Quote asset of the bot's markets, for example USDT.

fields.name: markets
fields.doc:
Markets the bot trades, as its version's money card names them, for
 example BTC-USDT.

fields.name: funding
fields.doc:
Where the bot's initial funding came from, and how much. Absent until
 the deploy flow records the deploy proposal the bot came from.

fields.name: uptime_ratio
fields.doc:
Share of the time since the bot was first deployed during which it was
 running, as an exact decimal from 0 to 1 rounded to 6 decimal places,
 for example "0.9875". A bot runs from each start to the stop the user
 recorded; time it spent paused counts as running. Empty before the bot
 first starts.

fields.name: running_since
fields.doc: When the bot last started running. Set only while it is RUNNING.

fields.name: pause_reason
fields.doc:
Why the bot paused. Set only with PAUSED, which is read only once the
 bot's pause has been reported to the service.

fields.name: activity
fields.doc:
What the bot did in each of the last 24 hours, oldest first, ending with
 the current UTC hour, which is still under way. An hour it did nothing
 in is there with zero counts. A bot deployed again within the day counts
 every one of its runs. Counts lag the bot by up to about a minute.

types.name: strategies.v1.BotActivityHour
types.doc:
BotActivityHour is what a bot did in one UTC hour, by when each event
 reached it.

fields.name: start
fields.doc: The hour's start: a whole UTC hour.

fields.name: decisions
fields.doc:
Its decisions: events the bot was called for, whether the call
 succeeded, failed, or ended before the bot's code ran.

fields.name: fills
fields.doc: Its fills, whether or not its code handles them.

fields.name: expired
fields.doc:
Events it skipped because they were already too old when it could run,
 for example while it was behind: never decisions.

types.name: strategies.v1.BotCapDetail
types.doc: BotCapDetail explains BOT_CAP_REACHED.

fields.name: vip_tier
fields.doc: The caller's current VIP tier.

fields.name: bot_cap
fields.doc: The most bots the tier allows at once.

fields.name: bots
fields.doc: Bots the caller runs now, deploying ones included.

fields.name: next_vip_tier
fields.doc: The next VIP tier with a higher cap. Zero when no tier lifts it.

fields.name: next_bot_cap
fields.doc: The cap of next_vip_tier. Zero when no tier lifts it.

types.name: strategies.v1.BotDecision
types.doc: BotDecision is one handler call of a bot.

fields.name: decided_at
fields.doc: When the event that woke the bot reached it.

fields.name: event
fields.doc: The handler the event woke, for example on_timer or on_fill.

fields.name: orders
fields.doc:
The orders the bot asked for, in the shape the manifest's behaviour
 examples use, with what a live call adds; a key is left out when unset.
 An order: {"buy" or "sell": market, "qty" or "quote", "limit", "tif",
 "post_only", "max_slippage_bps", "stop_loss", "take_profit", "reason",
 "client_order_id"}. A trigger (bot.buy_when, bot.sell_when): {"buy" or
 "sell": market, "above" or "below": its price, "qty", "limit", "tif",
 "price_source", "reason", "client_trigger_id"}. A cancel: {"cancel": the
 order's or trigger's client ID, or the trigger's ID}. An order refused
 before it was sent: {"refused": market, "client_order_id", "reason"}.
 Amounts and prices are decimal strings. An order on a market the
 service doesn't know names it "market #<id>", shows its amounts and
 prices as unscaled integers, and carries "unscaled": true. Empty when
 it decided to do nothing.

fields.name: logs
fields.doc:
The bot's log lines from the call, oldest first: at most 20, each at
 most 256 bytes of UTF-8 and 1 KiB in all. A shortened line ends with
 "…", and a last line of "…" stands for the lines left out.

types.name: strategies.v1.BotError
types.doc: BotError is one failed handler call of a bot.

fields.name: time
fields.doc: When the event whose call failed reached the bot.

fields.name: event
fields.doc: The handler the event woke, for example on_timer or on_fill.

fields.name: message
fields.doc:
What failed, at most 512 bytes of UTF-8, ending with "…" when
 shortened: the bot's own error when its code raised, the rule its result
 broke, or a sentence saying the call ran out of its time or memory or
 could not finish.

types.name: strategies.v1.BotFunding
types.doc:
BotFunding is where a bot's initial funding came from, as its deploy
 proposal recorded it.

fields.name: subaccount_id
fields.doc:
Public ID of the subaccount the funding came from. Zero means the main
 account.

Public ID. ConnectRPC carries it as fixed64 (a decimal string in JSON).

fields.name: subaccount_label
fields.doc:
Current label of that subaccount, as its owner named it. Empty for the
 main account or a subaccount without a label.

fields.name: initial_funding
fields.doc:
What moved into the bot's subaccount when it was deployed, one entry
 per asset.

types.name: strategies.v1.BotLogEntry
types.doc:
BotLogEntry is one entry of a bot's recent activity: a decision, a line its
 call wrote, or a failed call.

fields.name: sequence
fields.doc:
Position in the log of the bot's current deployment, increasing within
 that deployment. A new deployment starts a new log, whose positions start
 low again. A decision comes first, then the lines its call wrote, then
 its error if the call failed.

fields.name: time
fields.doc:
When the event behind it was observed: a decision's lines and its error
 have the decision's time. Two decisions can have the same time, for
 example two markets' candles of one minute.

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: What it records.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: The line.

types.name: strategies.v1.BotStatusCount
types.doc: BotStatusCount is how many of the caller's bots are in one status.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: The status.

fields.name: count
fields.doc: How many of the caller's bots are in it.

types.name: strategies.v1.BotVersion
types.doc: BotVersion is one run of a bot on one version.

fields.name: version_id
fields.doc: The version the bot ran. GetStrategyVersion reads it.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: The version's strategy name.

fields.name: runtime_version
fields.doc: Runtime version the version was validated against.

fields.name: started_at
fields.doc: When the bot started running this version.

fields.name: stopped_at
fields.doc:
When the stop of this run was recorded. Omitted while the run has no
 stop.

types.name: strategies.v1.CommunityBacktest
types.doc:
CommunityBacktest is a community listing's platform backtest: the backtest
 the platform starts of the published version when it is published, over
 the default window (the most recent 365 days of data), with the default
 settings, 1,000 of the quote asset and the standard fee schedule. Its
 author chooses none of these, so every listing's results compare alike.
 It is pinned to the publish: publishing a later version starts a new one,
 and nothing runs it again on a schedule. It is the platform's own run: it
 shows nothing of the author's own backtests.

fields.name: status
fields.doc:
Where it is. NOT_BACKTESTABLE when the bot can't be backtested on
 candles, which not_backtestable_reason explains; the listing then shows
 no results. FAILED when it ended without results, which failure
 explains: a backtest whose runs couldn't finish is run once more by the
 platform before it fails.

fields.name: not_backtestable_reason
fields.doc:
Why the bot can't be backtested. Set only when status is
 NOT_BACKTESTABLE.

fields.name: window
fields.doc:
The simulated window. Unset when status is NOT_BACKTESTABLE and the
 backtest never started.

fields.name: metrics
fields.doc:
The results over the report's period, for the base cost scenario: the
 report's metrics. Set only when status is DONE.

fields.name: report
fields.doc:
The whole result, as the platform's run made it. Set only by
 GetCommunityStrategy, when status is DONE.

fields.name: failure
fields.doc: Why it failed. Set only when status is FAILED.

types.name: strategies.v1.CommunityStrategy
types.doc:
CommunityStrategy is one public community listing with its published
 version: everything a reader needs to judge it, and nothing of its
 author's account. The settings shown are the version's defaults, never
 the author's own values.

fields.name: listing_id
fields.doc: Public listing ID.

fields.name: title
fields.doc: The listing's title.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: The listing's description.

fields.name: tags
fields.doc: The strategy's types.

fields.name: markets
fields.doc: The markets the published version trades, for example BTC-USDT.

fields.name: author_username
fields.doc: The author's current username.

fields.name: published_at
fields.doc: When the shown version was published.

fields.name: version_id
fields.doc: The published version's ID.

fields.name: runtime_version
fields.doc: The runtime version it was checked against.

fields.name: manifest
fields.doc: The published version's manifest.

fields.name: code
fields.doc: The published version's code.

fields.name: settings_form
fields.doc: The settings a user may change, with their defaults.

fields.name: money_card
fields.doc: The published version's money rules.

fields.name: flow
fields.doc:
The published version's flow: what wakes the bot, what it checks and
 what it may do. Unset for a version stored before flows existed.

fields.name: backtest
fields.doc: The platform backtest of the published version, with its report.

types.name: strategies.v1.CommunityStrategySummary
types.doc:
CommunityStrategySummary is one public community listing, as lists show
 it.

fields.name: listing_id
fields.doc: Public listing ID. GetCommunityStrategy reads the listing.

fields.name: title
fields.doc: The listing's title.

fields.name: tags
fields.doc: The strategy's types.

fields.name: markets
fields.doc: The markets the published version trades, for example BTC-USDT.

fields.name: author_username
fields.doc: The author's current username.

fields.name: backtest
fields.doc: The platform backtest of the published version, without its report.

fields.name: published_at
fields.doc: When the shown version was published.

types.name: strategies.v1.CreateStrategyRequest
types.doc: CreateStrategyRequest creates one strategy of the caller.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Name of the strategy.

fields.name: template_id
fields.doc:
A bot template, from ListStrategyTemplates: its manifest and code are
 checked and saved as revision 1.

fields.name: version_id
fields.doc:
One of the caller's own versions, saved as revision 1 of the new
 strategy.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.doc:
Client-chosen key, unique per caller, that makes the call idempotent: the
 same key and request return the strategy the first call created, as it
 stands now, and never create a second one; another request with the same
 key, a SaveDraftVersion's included, is IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Required.

types.name: strategies.v1.CreateStrategyResponse
types.doc: CreateStrategyResponse is the created strategy.

fields.name: strategy
fields.doc: The strategy, as it stands now.

fields.name: version
fields.doc: The check result of revision 1's version. Unset for a blank strategy.

types.name: strategies.v1.DataGap
types.doc: DataGap is a span with missing market data.

fields.name: market
fields.doc: Market, for example BTC-USDT.

fields.name: timeframe
fields.doc: Candle timeframe, for example 1h.

fields.name: window
fields.doc: The span without data.

fields.name: affected
fields.doc:
True when the bot was exposed across it: it held a position, watched a
 price level or had an order waiting on that market. What happened inside
 the gap is unknown, so the result is less certain.

types.name: strategies.v1.DeleteStrategyRequest
types.doc: DeleteStrategyRequest deletes one strategy of the caller.

fields.name: strategy_id
fields.doc: Public strategy ID.

types.name: strategies.v1.DeleteStrategyResponse
types.doc: DeleteStrategyResponse confirms the strategy is deleted.

types.name: strategies.v1.DeployBotRequest
types.doc: DeployBotRequest deploys one deploy proposal of the caller.

fields.name: proposal_id
fields.doc: Public proposal ID.

fields.name: subaccount_authorization
fields.doc:
The user's signed authorization for the bot's new subaccount. Needed
 only when the deploy creates a subaccount: without it, such a deploy
 answers SUBACCOUNT_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED. A deploy that reuses one of
 the caller's closed bot subaccounts ignores it.

types.name: strategies.v1.DeployBotResponse
types.doc: DeployBotResponse is the proposal's status when the call returns.

fields.name: status
fields.doc:
The status: DEPLOYING once the bot's start is recorded (the bot then
 starts without the user), LIVE, or FAILED with failed_at and failure.
 SETTING_ACCESS means the exchange is still applying the bot's limits, and
 FUNDING without wait that the funding is still reaching the bot's
 subaccount: call again. FUNDING with wait: do what wait says, then call
 again.

types.name: strategies.v1.DeployProposalSummary
types.doc:
DeployProposalSummary is what a deploy proposal binds, for showing beside
 its link.

fields.name: version_id
fields.doc: The version proposed.

fields.name: bot_name
fields.doc: The bot's name.

fields.name: money_card
fields.doc: What the bot may do with money.

fields.name: settings
fields.doc: Every setting, with its value, in settings-form order.

fields.name: funding_subaccount_id
fields.doc: The subaccount the funding comes from. Zero means the main account.

fields.name: funding
fields.doc: What moves into the bot's new subaccount from the funding account.

fields.name: scenarios_passed
fields.doc: Behaviour examples that passed.

fields.name: backtest
fields.doc:
The version's latest backtest. Omitted when the bot cannot be
 backtested; not_backtestable_reason then says why.

fields.name: strategy_id
fields.doc: The strategy the proposal came from. Zero once the strategy is deleted.

fields.name: revision
fields.doc:
The strategy's revision proposed, whose version is version_id. Zero once
 the strategy is deleted.

fields.name: not_backtestable_reason
fields.doc:
Why the bot was not backtested, when it cannot be: the deploy page tells
 the user before they approve. Unset when backtest is set.

types.name: strategies.v1.DeployStatus
types.doc: DeployStatus is where a deploy proposal is.

fields.name: proposal_id
fields.doc: Public proposal ID.

fields.name: state
fields.doc: Current step.

fields.name: step
fields.doc:
The current step as the user sees it, for example "Funding the
 account…".

fields.name: bot_id
fields.doc: Public ID of the bot. Zero until the bot exists.

fields.name: subaccount_id
fields.doc:
Public ID of the bot's subaccount. Zero until it exists.

Public ID. ConnectRPC carries it as fixed64 (a decimal string in JSON).

fields.name: failure
fields.doc:
Why the deploy stopped and what the user can do. Empty unless state is
 FAILED.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.doc: When the proposal expires if not deployed.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.doc: When the state last changed.

fields.name: failed_at
fields.doc:
The step the deploy failed in: VALIDATING, CREATING_SUBACCOUNT,
 SETTING_ACCESS, FUNDING or DEPLOYING. Set when a deploy fails, by the deploy flow, beside
 failure; unset in any other state.

fields.name: wait
fields.doc:
What a running deploy waits for from the user before it can go on.
 Unset when it waits for nothing. Calling DeployBot again once the user
 has done it continues the deploy.

types.name: strategies.v1.DeployWait
types.doc: DeployWait is what a running deploy waits for from the user.

fields.name: reason
fields.doc: What the user has to do.

fields.name: address
fields.doc:
WHITELIST_REQUIRED: the bot's subaccount's smart account address, the
 one to add to the internal whitelist. Empty for any other reason.

types.name: strategies.v1.EquityPoint
types.doc: EquityPoint is one point of a backtest's equity curve.

fields.name: time
fields.doc: The time, in simulated time.

fields.name: equity
fields.doc: The bot's equity, as an exact decimal in the quote asset.

fields.name: buy_and_hold_equity
fields.doc: Buy-and-hold's equity at the same time, from the same starting balance.

types.name: strategies.v1.ErrorCode
types.doc: ErrorCode identifies a Strategies API error.

values.name: VERSION_NOT_FOUND
values.doc:
No strategy version of the caller has this ID, or it expired. Another
 account's version is reported the same way.

values.name: BACKTEST_NOT_FOUND
values.doc: No backtest of the caller has this ID.

values.name: PROPOSAL_NOT_FOUND
values.doc: No deploy proposal of the caller has this ID.

values.name: BOT_NOT_FOUND
values.doc: No bot of the caller has this ID.

values.name: RUNTIME_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED
values.doc:
The requested runtime version is not offered. GetStrategyReference
 without a runtime version names the current one.

values.name: MANIFEST_TOO_LARGE
values.doc:
The manifest is larger than 65536 bytes (64 KiB), measured as compact
 JSON.

values.name: SETTINGS_INVALID
values.doc:
A setting is unknown to the version's settings form, or its value is not
 a valid value of its kind or lies outside its bounds. field_path names it.

values.name: FUNDING_INVALID
values.doc:
A funding or initial balance names an asset twice, or an asset the bot's
 markets do not trade. field_path names it.

values.name: VERSION_INVALID
values.doc:
The version did not validate: its check returned valid false. Fix the
 errors and save the draft again.

values.name: SCENARIOS_FAILING
values.doc:
A behaviour example of the version fails, or the examples were never
 run. RunScenarios shows each result.

values.name: BACKTEST_MISSING
values.doc:
The version has no finished backtest. A bot that cannot be backtested
 (NOT_BACKTESTABLE, for any of the NotBacktestableReason causes) is exempt:
 its proposal records why, and the deploy page tells the user before they
 approve. Not returned until backtests are available.

values.name: MARKET_NOT_ALLOWED
values.doc: A market of the bot is not open to bots. markets lists them.

values.name: INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS
values.doc:
The funding account does not hold the funding. shortfall gives the
 missing amounts.

values.name: BOT_CAP_REACHED
values.doc:
The caller already runs as many bots as their VIP tier allows. bot_cap
 gives the tier, the cap and the next tier's cap.

values.name: WINDOW_HAS_NO_DATA
values.doc:
The backtest window holds no market data for the bot's markets and
 timeframes.

values.name: NOT_BACKTESTABLE
values.doc:
The bot cannot be backtested on candles: it reacts to events candles do
 not carry, such as top-of-book or trade updates, or social signals; it
 reads trading volume, which the price history does not include; its
 markets have different quote assets; or a market it needs has no
 available price history at all. Only bots that trade with market orders,
 including exits on watched price levels, are backtested: a bot's first
 limit order ends its backtest as NOT_BACKTESTABLE. ExplainStrategy says
 so for what is known before a backtest runs: the events, markets and
 quote assets the bot reads. A limit order is found only while it runs.

values.name: SCENARIO_RUN_LIMIT_REACHED
values.doc:
The caller ran the most behaviour-example runs allowed per minute.
 retry_after says when to try again.

values.name: BACKTEST_LIMIT_REACHED
values.doc:
The caller started 200 backtests in the current UTC day, and retry_after
 says when the day resets (00:00 UTC); or the caller has 3 backtests
 queued or running, and retry_after is unset: one frees a slot when it
 finishes. A request that returns an existing backtest, by the same key
 or the same identity, never counts; starting a failed backtest again
 under a new key counts as a new start.

values.name: INDICATOR_SETTINGS_LIMIT_REACHED
values.doc:
The caller's bots and backtests would read more distinct indicator
 settings than allowed. Reuse an indicator setting another bot reads, or
 stop a bot. Not returned until the limit is enforced.

values.name: IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT
values.doc:
The idempotency key was already used with a different request. The
 original backtest, proposal, stop, strategy or saved draft stands.

values.name: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE
values.doc:
A required service is temporarily unavailable; retry the same request.
 Every call of this API is safe to retry.

values.name: FUNDING_SUBACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND
values.doc: The funding subaccount is not a subaccount of the caller's main account.

values.name: BOT_NOT_RUNNING
values.doc: The bot has already stopped.

values.name: BOT_ALREADY_STOPPING
values.doc:
The bot is already being stopped with the other stop mode. A bot is
 stopped once; its orders can still be cancelled directly.

values.name: STRATEGY_NOT_FOUND
values.doc:
No strategy of the caller has this ID. Another account's strategy is
 reported the same way.

values.name: DRAFT_REVISION_CONFLICT
values.doc:
The draft moved on since expected_revision: another save landed first.
 revision_conflict gives the current revision and its version. Read the
 strategy again, apply the change to its current draft, and save with
 the new revision.

values.name: STRATEGY_CAP_REACHED
values.doc:
The caller already has as many strategies as allowed. strategy_cap gives
 the cap.

values.name: TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND
values.doc: No bot template has this ID. ListStrategyTemplates lists them.

values.name: STRATEGY_IN_USE
values.doc:
The strategy is in use, so it can't be deleted: a bot deployed from it
 hasn't stopped, a deploy proposal of it is waiting to be deployed, or its
 community listing is public. Stop the bot, let the proposal expire, or
 unpublish the listing, and delete it again.

values.name: REVISION_NOT_FOUND
values.doc:
The strategy has no revision with this number. Revisions are numbered
 from 1, so zero is never one.

values.name: BACKTEST_NOT_DONE
values.doc:
The backtest hasn't finished, so it has no trades to list yet. Read its
 status with GetBacktest.

values.name: MFA_ELEVATION_REQUIRED
values.doc:
Deploying a bot needs a recently MFA-elevated session (MFA_RECENT).
 Complete MFA and deploy again; nothing was started.

values.name: PROPOSAL_EXPIRED
values.doc:
The deploy proposal expired before it was deployed. Propose the deploy
 again.

values.name: SUBACCOUNT_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED
values.doc:
The deploy needs a new subaccount, and the request carries no signed
 authorization for it, or one that can no longer be used: a challenge
 since replaced or expired. Request a new subaccount challenge, have the
 user sign it, and deploy again with it. The deploy keeps its progress.

values.name: NOTES_REVISION_CONFLICT
values.doc:
The strategy's notes were saved since expected_notes_revision: another
 save landed first. notes_conflict gives the notes' current revision.
 Read the notes again, apply the change to them, and save with the new
 revision.

values.name: LISTING_NOT_FOUND
values.doc:
No public community listing has this ID. A listing its author
 unpublished is reported the same way, and so is another account's
 listing to UnpublishStrategy.

values.name: LISTING_CAP_REACHED
values.doc:
The caller already has as many public community listings as allowed.
 listing_cap gives the cap. Unpublish a listing to publish another.

values.name: USERNAME_REQUIRED
values.doc:
Publishing shows the author by username, and the caller has none yet.
 Claim a username and publish again.

values.name: PUBLISH_LIMIT_REACHED
values.doc:
The caller published as many times as allowed in the current UTC day.
 retry_after says when the day resets (00:00 UTC).

types.name: strategies.v1.ErrorDetail
types.doc:
ErrorDetail is attached to Strategies API errors as an error detail of type
 strategies.v1.ErrorDetail.

fields.name: code
fields.doc: Stable error code.

fields.name: field_path
fields.doc:
Request field the error is about, as a field path such as
 settings[0].value or funding[1].asset. Set only with SETTINGS_INVALID,
 FUNDING_INVALID and MANIFEST_TOO_LARGE.

fields.name: retry_after
fields.doc:
When the same request may succeed. Set only with
 SCENARIO_RUN_LIMIT_REACHED, PUBLISH_LIMIT_REACHED, and with
 BACKTEST_LIMIT_REACHED for the daily limit.

fields.name: bot_cap
fields.doc: Set only with BOT_CAP_REACHED.

fields.name: markets
fields.doc:
Markets not open to bots, as the manifest names them. Set only with
 MARKET_NOT_ALLOWED.

fields.name: shortfall
fields.doc:
Amounts the funding account lacks, one per asset. Set only with
 INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS.

fields.name: strategy_cap
fields.doc: Set only with STRATEGY_CAP_REACHED.

fields.name: revision_conflict
fields.doc: Set only with DRAFT_REVISION_CONFLICT.

fields.name: not_backtestable_reason
fields.doc: Why the bot cannot be backtested. Set only with NOT_BACKTESTABLE.

fields.name: backtest_limit
fields.doc:
The caller's backtest limits and use. Set only with
 BACKTEST_LIMIT_REACHED.

fields.name: notes_conflict
fields.doc: Set only with NOTES_REVISION_CONFLICT.

fields.name: listing_cap
fields.doc: Set only with LISTING_CAP_REACHED.

types.name: strategies.v1.EvidenceGrade
types.doc:
EvidenceGrade is how much a backtest's result can be trusted: it follows
 from its closed trades, the days its market data fully covers, and its
 gaps, never from the calendar span alone.

values.name: NOT_ENOUGH
values.doc: Too few trades or too little covered data to judge.

values.name: LOW
values.doc: Some evidence.

values.name: MEDIUM
values.doc: Fair evidence.

values.name: HIGH
values.doc: Strong evidence.

types.name: strategies.v1.ExplainStrategyRequest
types.doc: ExplainStrategyRequest asks for the review summary of a version.

fields.name: version_id
fields.doc: Version to explain.

types.name: strategies.v1.ExplainStrategyResponse
types.doc:
ExplainStrategyResponse is what a user reviews before deploying a version.
 It is built from the manifest and the recorded results alone, so it states
 exactly what the user approves.

fields.name: version_id
fields.doc: The version explained.

fields.name: money_card
fields.doc: What the bot may do with money, its markets and its events.

fields.name: settings
fields.doc: The settings a user may change.

fields.name: scenarios
fields.doc: Each behaviour example and its last result, in manifest order.

fields.name: backtest
fields.doc:
The latest backtest. Omitted when there is none; backtest_absent_reason
 then says why.

fields.name: backtest_absent_reason
fields.doc:
Why there is no backtest, for example that the bot cannot be backtested
 on candles. Empty when backtest is set.

fields.name: warnings
fields.doc:
What to weigh before deploying, for example "never backtested" or "trades
 a thin market".

fields.name: limitations
fields.doc:
What the bot does not do, for example "stopping the bot does not sell its
 holdings".

types.name: strategies.v1.FlowEdge
types.doc: FlowEdge is one edge of a flow.

fields.name: from_node_id
fields.doc: The node it starts from.

fields.name: to_node_id
fields.doc: The node it leads to.

fields.name: branch
fields.doc: "true" or "false" out of a condition; empty otherwise.

types.name: strategies.v1.FlowNode
types.doc: FlowNode is one trigger, condition or action of a flow.

fields.name: node_id
fields.doc: Stable within the version, for example "t0", "c3" or "a1".

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: What it is.

fields.name: label
fields.doc:
What the node shows: a plain description of the code, for example
 "RSI(BTC-USDT, 1d, 14) > 75" or "Buy BTC-USDT for budget". For a
 trigger: a schedule in words, for example "Every Monday 09:00 UTC";
 another manifest event as the money card names it (the same text as
 event); otherwise what wakes the bot, for example "An order fills".

fields.name: span
fields.doc: Where it is in the code. Not set for a trigger.

fields.name: event
fields.doc:
For a trigger woken by a manifest event: the event, as the money card
 names it, for example "schedule mon 09:00 UTC". Empty otherwise.

fields.name: action
fields.doc:
For an action: BUY, SELL, CANCEL, LOG, NOTIFY, PAUSE, WATCH, UNWATCH or
 TRIGGER. Empty otherwise.

fields.name: settings
fields.doc: The settings the node reads, by name.

fields.name: backtest_id
fields.doc: Public backtest ID.

types.name: strategies.v1.GetBacktestResponse

fields.name: backtest
fields.doc: The backtest.

types.name: strategies.v1.GetBotRequest
types.doc: GetBotRequest reads one bot of the caller.

fields.name: bot_id
fields.doc: Public bot ID.

types.name: strategies.v1.GetBotResponse
types.doc:
GetBotResponse is a bot with its money rules, settings and recent
 decisions. The bot's subaccount is read like any other, by its
 subaccount_id: its balances with LedgerReadService.GetBalances, its open
 orders with OrdersReadService.GetOpenOrders, and its profit and loss with
 ProfitAndLossService.

fields.name: bot
fields.doc: The bot.

fields.name: money_card
fields.doc: What the bot may do with money, from the version it runs.

fields.name: settings
fields.doc:
Its settings, with their values, in settings-form order, each with its
 description, kind and asset from the version's settings form. Empty
 until the deploy flow records the deploy proposal the bot came from.

fields.name: decisions
fields.doc:
Its last decisions, newest first, from the run it is on now: at most 20,
 fewer when they are large. Empty until its run's first decision reaches
 the service, up to about a minute after the bot made it.

fields.name: errors
fields.doc: Its last errors, newest first, from the run it is on now: at most 20.

types.doc: GetCommunityStrategyRequest reads one public community listing.

fields.name: listing_id
fields.doc: Public listing ID.

types.name: strategies.v1.GetCommunityStrategyResponse

fields.name: strategy

 deploy page shows it.

fields.name: proposal_id

types.name: strategies.v1.GetDeployProposalResponse

fields.name: proposal_id
fields.doc: Public proposal ID.

fields.name: summary
fields.doc:
What the user approves: the version, the bot's name, its limits, every
 setting with its value, and the funding, as the proposal recorded them.

fields.name: status
fields.doc: Where the proposal is, and when it expires if not deployed.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When the proposal was recorded.

fields.name: funding_subaccount_label
fields.doc:
Current label of the subaccount the funding comes from, as its owner
 named it. Empty when the funding comes from the main account or the
 subaccount has no label.

types.name: strategies.v1.GetDeployStatusResponse

fields.name: status

types.name: strategies.v1.GetStrategyNotesResponse

fields.name: notes

types.name: strategies.v1.GetStrategyReferenceRequest
types.doc: GetStrategyReferenceRequest asks for what bot code is written against.

fields.name: runtime_version
fields.doc:
Runtime version to describe. Empty means the current one. One runtime
 version is offered; any other value is RUNTIME_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED.

types.name: strategies.v1.GetStrategyReferenceResponse
types.doc:
GetStrategyReferenceResponse is the bot format of one runtime version, and
 the skill pack for writing bots. Every field is always set.

fields.name: runtime_version
fields.doc: The runtime version described, for example 2026-11.

fields.name: indicator_library
fields.doc: The indicator library and its pinned version.

fields.name: reference
fields.doc:
The bot API reference as Markdown: events and handlers, the manifest,
 reads, actions, money rules, limits and language rules, with examples.

fields.name: manifest_schema
fields.doc:
JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of the manifest: its fields, their types and
 their bounds. The validation SaveDraftVersion runs is the authority, and
 also checks rules across fields, such as a market listed in markets or
 the markets' one quote asset, as the reference describes.

fields.name: indicators
fields.doc: Every indicator bot code may read.

fields.name: limits
fields.doc: Limits every bot of this runtime version runs under.

fields.name: skill_pack
fields.doc:
The skill pack: guidance for writing bots against the reference (the
 workflow, the language subset, patterns and pitfalls), one Markdown
 document per part, workflow first.

fields.name: skill_pack_version
fields.doc:
Version of the skill pack: "sha256:" followed by the lowercase hex
 SHA-256 of, for each document in skill_pack order, the UTF-8 bytes of its
 name and then of its Markdown, each preceded by its length in bytes as an
 unsigned 64-bit big-endian integer. It changes exactly when a document's
 name, content or position does.

types.name: strategies.v1.GetStrategyRequest
types.doc: GetStrategyRequest reads one strategy of the caller.

fields.name: strategy_id
fields.doc: Public strategy ID.

types.name: strategies.v1.GetStrategyResponse
types.doc: GetStrategyResponse is a strategy and its current draft.

fields.name: strategy
fields.doc: The strategy.

fields.name: head
fields.doc:
The version of the current revision, as GetStrategyVersion reads it.
 Unset when revision is zero.

fields.name: notes
fields.doc:
The strategy's notes, as GetStrategyNotes reads them: notes_revision is
 zero when they were never saved.

types.name: strategies.v1.GetStrategyVersionRequest
types.doc: GetStrategyVersionRequest reads one strategy version of the caller.

fields.name: version_id
fields.doc: Version to read.

types.name: strategies.v1.GetStrategyVersionResponse
types.doc:
GetStrategyVersionResponse is a stored strategy version: what a new
 strategy can start from.

fields.name: version_id
fields.doc: The version's ID.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Name of the strategy.

fields.name: runtime_version
fields.doc: The runtime version it was validated against.

fields.name: manifest
fields.doc: The manifest, as it was saved.

fields.name: code
fields.doc: The bot code.

fields.name: settings_form
fields.doc:
The settings a user may change. Empty when the version did not
 validate.

fields.name: valid
fields.doc: True when the version validated without errors.

fields.name: created_at
fields.doc: When the version was first stored.

fields.name: flow
fields.doc:
The version's flow: what wakes the bot, what it checks and what it may
 do. Not set for a version that did not validate, or that was stored
 before flows existed.

fields.name: validation
fields.doc:
The version's check result as it was stored, the same one saving the
 version answered: its errors and warnings, and, for a valid version, its
 money card, settings form and flow. Reading never checks the version
 again. Not set for a version stored without its check result.

types.name: strategies.v1.Indicator
types.doc: Indicator is one indicator bot code may read.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Indicator name, as bot code calls it, for example rsi.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: What the indicator measures.

fields.name: parameters
fields.doc: Parameters, in the order bot code passes them.

fields.name: outputs
fields.doc:
Output names, as bot code reads them: value first, then any others, for
 example value alone for RSI, or value (the middle band), upper and lower
 for Bollinger bands.

fields.name: warmup_bars
fields.doc:
Closed candles needed before the indicator has a value, as a sum of its
 parameter names and whole numbers joined by + and -, for example
 "period + 1". Until then bot code reads no value.

types.name: strategies.v1.IndicatorLibrary
types.doc:
IndicatorLibrary names the indicator library a runtime version computes
 indicators with.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Library name.

fields.name: version
fields.doc:
Exact library version, pinned for every bot deployed on the runtime
 version.

types.name: strategies.v1.IndicatorParameter
types.doc: IndicatorParameter is one parameter of an allowed indicator.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Parameter name, as bot code passes it, for example period.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: What the parameter sets.

fields.name: minimum
fields.doc: Smallest allowed value, as an exact decimal.

fields.name: maximum
fields.doc: Largest allowed value, as an exact decimal.

fields.name: default_value
fields.doc: Value used when bot code omits the parameter, as an exact decimal.

fields.name: integer
fields.doc: True when only whole numbers are allowed.

types.name: strategies.v1.ListBacktestTradesRequest
types.doc: ListBacktestTradesRequest reads one page of a finished backtest's trades.

fields.name: backtest_id
fields.doc: Public backtest ID.

fields.name: page_token
fields.doc:
Page token from a previous response; empty for the first page. It is
 opaque and exclusive: it carries the last trade_index returned, so the
 next page starts after it, and it is bound to the caller and the
 backtest it came from.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: Most trades to return, at most 1,000. Zero means 100.

types.name: strategies.v1.ListBacktestTradesResponse
types.doc: ListBacktestTradesResponse is one page of trades, in trade_index order.

fields.name: trades
fields.doc: The trades.

fields.name: next_page_token
fields.doc:
Token for the next page, after the last trade returned; empty on the
 last page. It is valid only for the same caller and backtest.

types.name: strategies.v1.ListBacktestsRequest
types.doc:
ListBacktestsRequest lists the backtests of one strategy of the caller:
 the backtests of the versions its revisions saved.

fields.name: strategy_id
fields.doc: Public strategy ID.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: Maximum number of backtests to return: default 10, max 50.

fields.name: page_token
fields.doc:
Opaque, keyset-backed and exclusive cursor from a previous response's
 next_page_token. It is bound to the caller and strategy_id; reuse it
 only with the same strategy_id.

types.name: strategies.v1.ListBacktestsResponse
types.doc: ListBacktestsResponse returns one page of a strategy's backtests.

fields.name: backtests
fields.doc: Backtests, newest first. A backtest is kept 30 days after it finished.

fields.name: next_page_token
fields.doc: Cursor for the next page. Empty when no more results exist.

types.name: strategies.v1.ListBotLogsRequest
types.doc: ListBotLogsRequest reads a bot's recent activity.

fields.name: bot_id
fields.doc: Public bot ID.

fields.name: start_time
fields.doc:
Earliest entry time, inclusive. Unset reads from the oldest entry kept.
 It filters by the time of the event behind each entry, which doesn't
 follow the order of the log: to read what is written later, use
 follow_token, never a later start_time.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: Maximum number of entries to return: default 100, max 200.

fields.name: page_token
fields.doc:
Opaque, keyset-backed and exclusive cursor from a previous response's
 next_page_token, or follow_token. It is bound to the caller, bot_id,
 start_time and the deployment whose log the first page read; reuse it
 only with the same values. Its pages read that deployment's log even
 after the bot is deployed again.

types.name: strategies.v1.ListBotLogsResponse
types.doc: ListBotLogsResponse returns one page of a bot's recent activity.

fields.name: entries
fields.doc: Entries, oldest first: in increasing sequence.

fields.name: next_page_token
fields.doc: Cursor for the next page. Empty when no more results exist now.

fields.name: follow_token
fields.doc:
Cursor for what is written later: pass it as page_token, now or later,
 to read the entries after the last one this response read, by sequence,
 in the same deployment's log. Set on the last page. An entry that left
 the window before it was read is not returned.

fields.name: deployed_again
fields.doc:
The bot was deployed again after the deployment whose log this response
 read: a new run started, whose entries are in a new log, read by listing
 again without page_token. It doesn't end this log: entries of this
 deployment can still arrive after it, with no set time limit, and
 follow_token keeps reading them for as long as they are kept.

fields.name: bot_id
fields.doc: Public bot ID.

fields.name: page_token

Opaque, keyset-backed and exclusive cursor from a previous response's

types.name: strategies.v1.ListBotVersionsResponse

fields.name: versions

One entry per run of the bot, newest started first: a version deployed

fields.name: next_page_token

types.name: strategies.v1.ListBotsResponse

fields.name: bots

fields.name: next_page_token

fields.name: status_counts
fields.doc:
How many of all the caller's bots, not only this page's, are in each
 status: one entry per status that has a bot, in status order. Exact when
 read, and the same shape on every page. Not a pagination total.

types.name: strategies.v1.ListCommunityStrategiesRequest
types.doc: ListCommunityStrategiesRequest lists the public community listings.

fields.name: tags
fields.doc: Only listings with any of these types. Empty lists every type.

fields.name: markets

Only listings trading any of these markets, each by its symbol, for

 is refused, never matched against no listing.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: Maximum number of listings to return: default 20, max 100.

fields.name: page_token
fields.doc:
Opaque, keyset-backed and exclusive cursor from a previous response's
 next_page_token. It is bound to tags and markets; reuse it only with the
 same values.

ListCommunityStrategiesResponse returns one page of public community

fields.name: strategies

Listings, most recently published first, then by listing ID,
 descending.

types.name: strategies.v1.ListStrategiesResponse

fields.name: strategies

ListStrategyNotesRevisionsRequest lists the saved notes of one strategy of

types.name: strategies.v1.StartBacktestRequest
types.doc:
StartBacktestRequest starts a backtest of a version.

 A retry is bound by idempotency_key: the same key and request return the
 backtest the first request started, even when an unset window bound would
 now resolve differently, and never count again against the backtest quota
 or the attempts.

 Across keys, a backtest's identity is its version, effective window,
 effective settings, effective initial balances, and what the platform
 resolves when the request arrives: the caller's fee rates, the platform's
 spread, slippage and fill assumptions, and the simulation's versions. A
 request whose identity matches an earlier backtest of the caller returns
 that backtest rather than running again, so a request that spells out a
 default refers to the same run, while a request that changes any of them,
 or arrives after the platform's part changed, starts a new one:
 - effective window: start_time and end_time, each floored to a whole
   second; an unset end is the end of the longest window with data when
   the request arrives, and an unset start is 365 days before the window's
   end, or fewer for a bot whose candle, schedule and on_start calls would
   not fit a backtest's calls (see start_time), or the start of that
   longest window when its data is shorter;
 - effective settings: every setting of the version's settings form, by
   name, with its default value where the request leaves it out;
 - effective initial balances: initial_balances, or when it is empty,
   1,000 of the bot's quote asset; one per asset, sorted by asset;
 - every decimal in its canonical form, without leading zeros or trailing
   fractional zeros, so "50", "50.0" and "050" are the same amount.

fields.name: version_id
fields.doc: Version to backtest.

fields.name: start_time
fields.doc:
Start of the window, inclusive, floored to a whole second. Unset means
 the most recent 365 days of data: 365 days before the window's end, or
 the start of the longest window with data for the bot's markets and
 timeframes when that is shorter. A backtest holds at most 30,000 calls
 of the bot, across its three cost scenarios. When the bot's code
 handles candles, each close of a candle series it declares under
 candles is a call in each scenario; when it handles its schedule, each
 firing is one; and on_start, when the code defines it, is one at the
 start of each. Unset keeps 365 days only when all of those calls
 together, over 365 days, fit; otherwise it means the most whole days
 whose calls fit, at least one. The calls combine: a bot on one series of
 minute candles alone gets 6 days, on two 3, on a 15-minute schedule
 alone 104, and on an hourly series with an hourly schedule 208, though
 either of those alone keeps 365 days. Only those calls are sized: calls
 the bot gets from its orders and price levels can still take a backtest
 past its calls, as can a bot too busy for even one day.

fields.name: end_time
fields.doc:
End of the window, exclusive, floored to a whole second. Unset means the
 end of that longest window.

fields.name: settings
fields.doc:
Values for the version's settings form, at most 64, each setting once.
 Settings left out take their default value.

fields.name: initial_balances
fields.doc:
Starting balances of the simulated account, one per asset of the bot's
 markets, each amount more than 0: a zero or negative amount is
 FUNDING_INVALID. Empty, whether left out or sent as an empty list, means
 1,000 of the bot's quote asset, for example 1000 USDT, whatever its
 settings, such as a budget that is the amount of each buy. Part of the
 backtest's identity: the same run with other balances is another
 backtest.

fields.name: idempotency_key
fields.doc:
Client-chosen key, unique per caller, that makes the call idempotent: the
 same key and request return the backtest the first call started; another
 request with the same key is IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.

types.name: strategies.v1.StartBacktestResponse
types.doc: StartBacktestResponse is the started backtest.

fields.name: status
fields.doc:
Status: QUEUED for a new backtest, or the current status of the same
 backtest started before.

fields.name: estimated_seconds
fields.doc: Estimated seconds until it finishes.

fields.doc: The version saved. GetStrategyVersion reads it.

fields.name: valid
fields.doc: True when the version validated without errors.

fields.name: saved_at
fields.doc: When the draft was saved.

fields.name: saved_by
fields.doc: How the caller that saved it signed in.

types.name: strategies.v1.StrategyTag
types.doc:
StrategyTag is a community strategy's type, from a fixed list. Markets are
 never tags: a listing's markets come from its version.

values.name: TREND
values.doc: Follows a price trend.

values.name: MEAN_REVERSION
values.doc: Trades a price back towards its average.

values.name: GRID
values.doc: Buys and sells on a grid of price levels.

values.name: DCA
values.doc: Buys a fixed amount on a schedule (dollar-cost averaging).

values.name: MARKET_MAKING
values.doc: Quotes both sides of a market.

values.name: ARBITRAGE
values.doc: Trades price differences between markets.

values.name: SIGNALS
values.doc: Trades on signals.

types.name: strategies.v1.StrategyTemplate
types.doc: StrategyTemplate is a starting point for a bot.

fields.name: template_id
fields.doc: Stable template ID, for example weekly-dca.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: Display name.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: What the template's bot does.

fields.name: manifest
fields.doc: The template's manifest, as SaveDraftVersion takes it.

fields.name: code
fields.doc: The template's bot code.

fields.name: runtime_version
fields.doc: Runtime version the template is written for.

fields.name: money_card
fields.doc:
What the template's bot may do with money, the markets it trades and the
 events it handles: the card a version saved from the template unchanged
 shows.

types.name: strategies.v1.SubaccountAuthorization
types.doc:
SubaccountAuthorization is the user's signed authorization for the bot's
 new subaccount: what CreateSubaccountChallenge returned, signed through the
 returned smart account.

fields.name: smart_account_address
fields.doc: The smart account address CreateSubaccountChallenge returned.

fields.name: message
fields.doc:
The exact message CreateSubaccountChallenge returned, unaltered. At most
 4096 bytes.

fields.name: signature
fields.doc:
The smart account's signature over message, with EIP-191 personal_sign
 semantics. At most 8192 characters.

types.name: strategies.v1.TimeWindow
types.doc: TimeWindow is a span of time: start_time inclusive, end_time exclusive.

fields.name: start_time
fields.doc: Start of the window, inclusive.

fields.name: end_time
fields.doc: End of the window, exclusive.

types.name: strategies.v1.UnpublishStrategyRequest
types.doc:
UnpublishStrategyRequest unpublishes one of the caller's community
 listings.

fields.name: listing_id
fields.doc: Public listing ID.

types.name: strategies.v1.UnpublishStrategyResponse
types.doc: UnpublishStrategyResponse is the unpublished listing.

fields.name: listing
fields.doc: The listing, as the author's strategy shows it: HIDDEN.

types.name: strategies.v1.ValidationIssue
types.doc: ValidationIssue is one problem a version's check found.

fields.name: manifest_path
fields.doc:
Path of the manifest value at fault, for example limits.max_order.amount.
 Empty when the issue is in the code.

fields.name: line
fields.doc:
Line of the code at fault, from 1. Zero when the issue is in the
 manifest.

fields.name: column
fields.doc:
Column of the code at fault, from 1. Zero when unknown or when the issue
 is in the manifest.

fields.name: rule
fields.doc:
Stable rule identifier, for example UNSUPPORTED_SYNTAX, UNKNOWN_CALL,
 MISSING_REASON, LIMIT_ABOVE_MAXIMUM or SCENARIO_UNPARSEABLE. A runtime
 version may add rules.

fields.name: message
fields.doc: What is wrong.

fields.name: hint
fields.doc: What to change to fix it.

types.name: strategies.v1.VersionValidation
types.doc:
VersionValidation is a version's check result: whether the bot is valid,
 its errors and warnings, and what it may do with money.

fields.name: version_id
fields.doc:
ID of the stored version, derived from the runtime version, manifest and
 code: the same content always gets the same ID.

fields.name: runtime_version
fields.doc: The runtime version validated against.

fields.name: valid
fields.doc: True when the bot has no errors.

fields.name: errors
fields.doc:
Errors, in code and manifest order: at most 50. Further errors may show
 once these are fixed.

fields.name: warnings
fields.doc: Warnings, in the same order and shape: at most 50.

fields.name: money_card
fields.doc: What the bot may do with money. Set only when valid.

fields.name: settings_form
fields.doc: The settings a user may change. Set only when valid.

fields.name: flow
fields.doc:
What wakes the bot, what it checks and what it may do, read from its
 code and manifest. Set only when valid.
